hypotheses.statement: For the two TP1/DP4/EP4 engines, first inspect the effective image, router policy, API2 request path, and internal DP rank selection to establish whether rank-aware prefix routing is already active. If absent, test a bounded policy that prefers a rank holding an exact reusable prefix only while its estimated queue load stays within a chosen skew limit; otherwise it falls back to load-only routing. API2 must preserve or convey the rank choice through the internal DP4 decision, since replica affinity alone cannot guarantee a local cache hit. The 75% cacheability figure is a target, not an observed hit rate. Shadow routing should first determine whether avoidable rank-local misses exist. Predict better goodput only where saved prefill work outweighs skew and routing cost.
hypotheses.observed_bottleneck: Unknown. The supplied R7b closed-loop results are 27.69 req/s and 18.30s E2E p95 at c384, and 33.76 req/s and 19.49s at c512; they do not identify routing or cache misses as the bottleneck.
hypotheses.mechanism: Exact rank-local prefix reuse can avoid recomputation, while a load-skew cap and load-only fallback limit affinity-induced queueing.
hypotheses.proposed_change: After the presence gate, add or configure API2-to-DP-rank prefix-aware selection with an explicit skew cap, deterministic compatible hashes, and load-only fallback. Change routing alone before combining it with scheduler changes.
hypotheses.code_surface: API2 router, rank identity and targeting, V1 internal DP load balancer, prefix block hashing, routing telemetry.
hypotheses.applicability: Potentially useful for repeated exact prefixes resident on a DP rank; benefit is unknown for the B200 workload and can reverse when recoverable prefix work is small.
hypotheses.predicted_direction: Conditional increase in SLO goodput and served rank-local KV hits, with no unacceptable E2E p95 or cost per successful request regression; no effect size predicted.

alternatives.explanation: The desired cacheability may not produce resident exact-prefix hits, so routing cannot save meaningful prefill work.
alternatives.distinguishing_test: In shadow replay, compare cacheability labels with actual eligible exact-block residency and counterfactual rank-local hits.

alternatives.explanation: Affinity may overload a hot rank, offsetting saved prefill.
alternatives.distinguishing_test: Vary only the skew cap and inspect per-rank queue delay, served hits, and tail latency.

novelty.scientific: No novelty claim; bounded cache affinity is established prior work.
novelty.implementation: The possible delta is verified API2-to-internal-rank targeting and a bounded fallback in this deployment; current presence is unknown.
novelty.workload: Two engines with internal DP4 and agent-f75 plus Mooncake replay; actual prefix hits and rank skew are unknown.
novelty.nearest_prior_art: vLLM PR 43483 proposes internal DP prefix-aware routing; PR 58757 describes individual-engine affinity; CacheRoute discusses affinity versus load.
novelty.specific_delta: Conditionally connect exact-rank affinity to the R7b API2 path with a measurable skew bound, if inspection shows the capability is absent.

experiment.control: LAT-2XDEP4-R7b as actually running, plus the strongest tuned static routing policy selected on a calibration split, including load-only and fixed affinity candidates.
experiment.treatment: Bounded rank-aware prefix routing, with all engine and scheduler settings fixed.
experiment.metrics: Frozen length-aware SLO goodput; cost per successful request; E2E and TTFT p95; ITL p95 by output-length cohort; completed throughput; served exact rank-local KV hits; per-rank load and skew.
experiment.supports_if: On held-out replay, actual served rank-local hits rise and frozen SLO goodput improves over both controls without violating the predeclared skew and latency bounds.
experiment.rejects_if: Eligible exact-prefix hits are negligible, or load skew and queue delay erase the gain, or either strong control has better frozen SLO goodput.
experiment.inconclusive_if: The effective baseline policy or rank targeting cannot be established, cache-hit instrumentation is unreliable, or the replay lacks enough repeated resident prefixes.
experiment.held_out_condition: Mooncake median, burst, and cache-heavy traces with unseen skew and prefix distributions and request lengths, preserving output-length cohorts.
experiment.correctness: Verify compatible block hashes, exact rank identity, deterministic routing where required, and unchanged generated outputs. Do not infer a cache hit from routing choice alone.
experiment.cost: First inspect configuration and route decisions, then run a CPU-only shadow replay; GPU replay is a later test and is not requested now.

hypotheses.statement: First inspect the effective scheduler commit and runtime settings to establish whether adaptive prefill admission already exists. If absent, test a scheduler-local prefill budget that decreases when active decodes approach their measured iteration deadlines and increases when decode pressure eases. Keep the global token budget fixed; bound each prefill request’s waiting time so decode protection cannot starve TTFT. This transfers the pressure-dependent budget mechanism described by P-PAS, while adding an explicit deadline and waiting bound for the R7b objective. The source reports results on other model and GPU configurations, so neither a B200 crossover nor an effect size is known. A cheap trace analysis should first test whether prefill-bearing iterations coincide with decode deadline misses before any GPU replay.
hypotheses.observed_bottleneck: Unknown. The R7b baseline gives throughput and E2E p95, but no measured prefill interference, decode deadline misses, TTFT, or starvation.
hypotheses.mechanism: Limit admitted prefill work during decode pressure to reduce long mixed iterations, while releasing the cap when pressure falls or a prefill wait bound is reached.
hypotheses.proposed_change: After the presence gate, add an optional V1 scheduler admission budget using current decode deadline slack and prefill pressure, with a maximum wait bound and fixed-budget fallback. Test this factor independently of routing.
hypotheses.code_surface: V1 scheduler prefill admission, per-iteration timing telemetry, decode deadline estimate, per-request wait accounting.
hypotheses.applicability: Potentially useful if mixed prefill-decode iterations cause deadline misses in the target; the B200 response and safe admission bounds are unknown.
hypotheses.predicted_direction: Conditional reduction in decode ITL deadline misses and higher SLO goodput, while TTFT and starvation remain within chosen bounds; no numerical gain predicted.

alternatives.explanation: Decode delays may mainly reflect KV pressure, preemption, or another source rather than prefill admission.
alternatives.distinguishing_test: Attribute missed decode deadlines in traces to prefill-bearing iterations, preemption events, and queueing before implementing the controller.

alternatives.explanation: A single well-tuned static token budget or cadence may already achieve the same tradeoff.
alternatives.distinguishing_test: Compare against the best static budget and eligible fixed cadence chosen on a calibration split, then evaluate on held-out load regimes.

novelty.scientific: No novelty claim; adaptive prefill budgets and deadline-aware chunking are prior work.
novelty.implementation: The possible delta is a deadline and wait-bounded admission policy in the verified R7b scheduler, if absent.
novelty.workload: Long-input agent-f75 and Mooncake mixed-load replay; actual decode interference and B200 effect are unknown.
novelty.nearest_prior_art: P-PAS RFC and paper propose pressure-adaptive prefill budgets; the deadline-aware chunking paper and decode-priority cadence PR identify related tradeoffs.
novelty.specific_delta: Tie prefill admission to observed decode deadline slack and an explicit per-request waiting bound, then compare with the strongest static setting.

experiment.control: LAT-2XDEP4-R7b as actually running, plus the strongest static max_num_batched_tokens or eligible fixed cadence selected on a calibration split under the same scorer.
experiment.treatment: Deadline-aware adaptive prefill admission with a predeclared maximum wait bound; routing and other factors held fixed.
experiment.metrics: Frozen length-aware SLO goodput; cost per successful request; E2E and TTFT p95; ITL p95 by output-length cohort; completed throughput; decode deadline misses; prefill wait tail and starvation count.
experiment.supports_if: Held-out mixed-load replay shows fewer decode deadline misses and better frozen SLO goodput than both controls while respecting the predeclared TTFT and waiting bounds.
experiment.rejects_if: The cheap trace check finds no association between prefill admission and deadline misses, or the strongest static control matches or exceeds goodput, or TTFT and waiting bounds fail.
experiment.inconclusive_if: Runtime policy presence is unknown, timing traces cannot separate interference from preemption, or the held-out replay lacks mixed prefill-decode pressure.
experiment.held_out_condition: Mooncake median and burst traces plus unseen prompt and output-length mixes, including low-pressure periods and sustained prefill queues.
experiment.correctness: Confirm each admitted request progresses within the wait bound and generated outputs remain unchanged; measure whole-trace inter-token gaps separately from per-request TPOT.
experiment.cost: First inspect scheduler configuration and analyze existing traces without GPU execution; later conduct one-factor replay and a bounded static-policy sweep.

gaps: The effective image, commit, dirty tree, router policy, DP-rank targeting, and adaptive scheduler presence are unknown.
The 75% cacheability target is not an observed cache-hit rate; exact rank-local hits, load skew, decode deadline misses, TTFT, and starvation are unknown.
The supplied baseline profile is desired state rather than verified runtime state. Its reported measurements do not establish a causal bottleneck.

The cited routing PR reports tests but no serving effect; the documentation PR supplies no implementation evidence. P-PAS and cadence results are author reports from other configurations, with unknown transfer effect on eight B200 GPUs.
Freeze the length-aware scorer and output-length cohorts before comparison; its goodput differs from AIPerf goodput.
